paragraphs.text: וַיְהִ֗י אַחַר֙ הַדְּבָרִ֣ים הָאֵ֔לֶּה חָֽטְא֛וּ מַשְׁקֵ֥ה מֶֽלֶךְ־מִצְרַ֖יִם וְהָאֹפֶ֑ה לַאֲדֹנֵיהֶ֖ם לְמֶ֥לֶךְ מִצְרָֽיִם׃

i18n.en: And it came to pass after these things, that the butler of the king of Mitsrayim and his baker offended their lord the king of Mitsrayim.

notes.official: *Mashqeh* (מַשְׁקֶה), here rendered ASV-baseline **butler**, is a participial noun from the root *sh-q-h* ('to give drink') — literally **'one who gives drink', a cupbearer**: the court official who served and tasted the king's wine, a position of intimate royal access. Modern versions (NRSV, NJPS, Alter) prefer the more literal and more accurate 'cupbearer'; the older English 'butler' (KJV/ASV) is retained on the surface per the baseline convention. *Ofeh* (אֹפֶה), 'baker', is the participle of *a-f-h* ('to bake') and is uncontested. The two officials and their elevated *sar ha-X* titles (*sar ha-mashqim* / *sar ha-ofim*, v 2) are governed by `sar-ha-mashqim-sar-ha-ofim-chief-cupbearer-baker`, parallel to the already-central `sar-ha-tabbachim`; the cupbearer-and-baker pairing reflects an authentic Egyptian-court-milieu detail (Vergote *Joseph en Égypte* 1959; Redford VTSup 20, 1970).

paragraphs.text: וַיִּקְצֹ֣ף פַּרְעֹ֔ה עַ֖ל שְׁנֵ֣י סָרִיסָ֑יו עַ֚ל שַׂ֣ר הַמַּשְׁקִ֔ים וְעַ֖ל שַׂ֥ר הָאוֹפִֽים׃

i18n.en: And Pharaoh was wroth against his two officers, against the chief of the butlers, and against the chief of the bakers.

notes.official: The two men are Pharaoh's *sarisim* (sing. *saris*) — rendered ASV-baseline **officers** in the court-official sense per the established `saris-court-official-eunuch-ambiguity` entry (the *ša rēši* administrative-title etymology and the court-official-vs-eunuch ambiguity are documented there; the entry's *appliesTo* is extended to add Gen 40:2 and 40:7). Their titles, *sar ha-mashqim* ('chief of the butlers/cupbearers') and *sar ha-ofim* ('chief of the bakers'), are the *sar ha-X* office-title construction governed by `sar-ha-mashqim-sar-ha-ofim-chief-cupbearer-baker`.

paragraphs.text: וַיִּתֵּ֨ן אֹתָ֜ם בְּמִשְׁמַ֗ר בֵּ֛ית שַׂ֥ר הַטַבָּחִ֖ים אֶל־בֵּ֣ית הַסֹּ֑הַר מְק֕וֹם אֲשֶׁ֥ר יוֹסֵ֖ף אָס֥וּר שָֽׁם׃

i18n.en: And he put them in ward in the house of the captain of the guard, into the prison, the place where Yosef was bound.

notes.official: Two standing court-titles from the Yosef cycle reappear: the *sar ha-tabbachim* ('captain of the guard', Potifar's office, governed by `sar-ha-tabbachim-captain-of-the-guard`) and the *beit ha-sohar* ('the prison', the *sohar* round-house / loanword crux, governed by `beit-ha-sohar-prison-round-house`) — the same prison of Gen 39:20-23 where Yosef was confined. Both central entries' *appliesTo* arrays are extended (scope-formalization) to cover the Gen 40 occurrences (*sar ha-tabbachim* at vv 3-4; *beit ha-sohar* at vv 3, 5). No surface change: ASV-baseline 'captain of the guard' and 'prison' stand.

paragraphs.text: וַ֠יִּפְקֹד שַׂ֣ר הַטַּבָּחִ֧ים אֶת־יוֹסֵ֛ף אִתָּ֖ם וַיְשָׁ֣רֶת אֹתָ֑ם וַיִּהְי֥וּ יָמִ֖ים בְּמִשְׁמָֽר׃

i18n.en: And the captain of the guard charged Yosef with them, and he ministered unto them: and they continued a season in ward.

paragraphs.text: וַיַּֽחַלְמוּ֩ חֲל֨וֹם שְׁנֵיהֶ֜ם אִ֤ישׁ חֲלֹמוֹ֙ בְּלַ֣יְלָה אֶחָ֔ד אִ֖ישׁ כְּפִתְר֣וֹן חֲלֹמ֑וֹ הַמַּשְׁקֶ֣ה וְהָאֹפֶ֗ה אֲשֶׁר֙ לְמֶ֣לֶךְ מִצְרַ֔יִם אֲשֶׁ֥ר אֲסוּרִ֖ים בְּבֵ֥ית הַסֹּֽהַר׃

i18n.en: And they dreamed a dream both of them, each man his dream, in one night, each man according to the interpretation of his dream, the butler and the baker of the king of Mitsrayim, who were bound in the prison.

notes.official: First occurrence of the chapter's keyword *pitron* (פִּתְרוֹן) — the **interpretation / solution / decoding** of a dream — here *ish ke-fitron chalomo* ('each man according to the interpretation of his dream'). The noun *pitron* and its cognate verb *p-t-r* are near-exclusive to Gen 40-41 in the Hebrew Bible (the noun occurs only here and at 41:11), marking the dream-cycle as a self-contained novella with its own technical vocabulary; the root is cognate to the Aramaic *pesher* of Daniel. Governed by `pitron-dream-interpretation-yosef-cycle`. Note that *chalom* here is the **symbolic, puzzle-dream** requiring decoding — categorically distinct from the dream-as-direct-divine-address of the `divine-dream-communication-formula` entry (Gen 20:3, 31:24), which is correctly **not** applied to these dreams: nothing speaks *in* the Gen 40 dreams; their meaning is hidden and must be solved.

paragraphs.text: וַיָּבֹ֧א אֲלֵיהֶ֛ם יוֹסֵ֖ף בַּבֹּ֑קֶר וַיַּ֣רְא אֹתָ֔ם וְהִנָּ֖ם זֹעֲפִֽים׃

i18n.en: And Yosef came in unto them in the morning, and saw them, and, behold, they were sad.

notes.official: *Zo'afim* (זֹעֲפִים), the participle of *za'af*, rendered ASV-baseline **sad**. The root elsewhere carries a stronger **vexation / agitation / indignation** register (King Asa *za'af* in a rage, 2 Chr 16:10; Uzziah *za'af* furious, 2 Chr 26:19; the raging sea, Jonah 1:15), so the affect is debated between dejection and agitation; in context (men disturbed by undecoded dreams) the downcast 'sad' reading is natural and is the older-English choice. Governed by the overlay entry `zoafim-troubled-faces-cupbearer-baker-gen40`. At v 7 Yosef glosses their look as *penekhem ra'im* ('your faces look bad').

paragraphs.text: וַיִּשְׁאַ֞ל אֶת־סְרִיסֵ֣י פַרְעֹ֗ה אֲשֶׁ֨ר אִתּ֧וֹ בְמִשְׁמַ֛ר בֵּ֥ית אֲדֹנָ֖יו לֵאמֹ֑ר מַדּ֛וּעַ פְּנֵיכֶ֥ם רָעִ֖ים הַיּֽוֹם׃

i18n.en: And he asked Pharaoh's officers that were with him in ward in his master's house, saying, Wherefore look ye so sad to-day?

notes.official: The two men are again *seris(ei) Par'oh* — 'Pharaoh's officers' (court-official sense; `saris-court-official-eunuch-ambiguity`, *appliesTo* extended to add this verse). *Penekhem ra'im ha-yom* ('your faces look bad today') restates the *zo'afim* of v 6.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּאמְר֣וּ אֵלָ֔יו חֲל֣וֹם חָלַ֔מְנוּ וּפֹתֵ֖ר אֵ֣ין אֹת֑וֹ וַיֹּ֨אמֶר אֲלֵהֶ֜ם יוֹסֵ֗ף הֲל֤וֹא לֵֽאלֹהִים֙ פִּתְרֹנִ֔ים סַפְּרוּ־נָ֖א לִֽי׃

i18n.en: And they said unto him, We have dreamed a dream, and there is none that can interpret it. And Yosef said unto them, Do not interpretations belong to Elohim? tell it me, I pray you.

notes.official:
*Ein poter oto* ('there is none that can interpret it', the verb *p-t-r*) and Yosef's reply *ha-lo le-Elohim pitronim* ('Do not interpretations belong to Elohim?', the noun *pitron*, plural *pitronim*) are the chapter's keyword-cluster; the verse claims that the *decoding-capacity* — not the dream itself — is Elohim's gift, the dream-cycle's distinctive theology of interpretation. Governed by `pitron-dream-interpretation-yosef-cycle`.

The divine name here is **Elohim**, not YHWH — Yosef's own mouth, exactly as at Gen 39:9 (*ve-chatati le-Elohim*). Genesis 40's single divine-name occurrence is Elohim, the Yosef-cycle's Elohim-default reasserting itself the moment the narrative leaves the YHWH-saturated Gen 39 (the only Yosef-cycle chapter with a YHWH narrator-frame). This is a confirming scope-extension of the cycle-wide observation in `yosef-cycle-divine-name-alternation-yhwh-elohim` (overlay *appliesTo* extended to add Gen 40:8); the documentary-critical reading (Elohistic novella; Wellhausen, von Rad, Westermann, Coats, Redford, Friedman) is recorded there as named scholarship. The name is rendered exactly as the text has it; no harmonization.

paragraphs.text: וַיְסַפֵּ֧ר שַֽׂר־הַמַּשְׁקִ֛ים אֶת־חֲלֹמ֖וֹ לְיוֹסֵ֑ף וַיֹּ֣אמֶר ל֔וֹ בַּחֲלוֹמִ֕י וְהִנֵּה־גֶ֖פֶן לְפָנָֽי׃

i18n.en: And the chief butler told his dream to Yosef, and said to him, In my dream, behold, a vine was before me;

paragraphs.text: וּבַגֶּ֖פֶן שְׁלֹשָׁ֣ה שָׂרִיגִ֑ם וְהִ֤יא כְפֹרַ֙חַת֙ עָלְתָ֣ה נִצָּ֔הּ הִבְשִׁ֥ילוּ אַשְׁכְּלֹתֶ֖יהָ עֲנָבִֽים׃

i18n.en: and in the vine were three branches: and it was as though it budded, and its blossoms shot forth; and the clusters thereof brought forth ripe grapes:

paragraphs.text: וְכ֥וֹס פַּרְעֹ֖ה בְּיָדִ֑י וָאֶקַּ֣ח אֶת־הָֽעֲנָבִ֗ים וָֽאֶשְׂחַ֤ט אֹתָם֙ אֶל־כּ֣וֹס פַּרְעֹ֔ה וָאֶתֵּ֥ן אֶת־הַכּ֖וֹס עַל־כַּ֥ף פַּרְעֹֽה׃

i18n.en: and Pharaoh's cup was in my hand; and I took the grapes, and pressed them into Pharaoh's cup, and I gave the cup into Pharaoh's hand.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר לוֹ֙ יוֹסֵ֔ף זֶ֖ה פִּתְרֹנ֑וֹ שְׁלֹ֙שֶׁת֙ הַשָּׂ֣רִגִ֔ים שְׁלֹ֥שֶׁת יָמִ֖ים הֵֽם׃

i18n.en: And Yosef said unto him, This is the interpretation of it: the three branches are three days;

paragraphs.text: בְּע֣וֹד ׀ שְׁלֹ֣שֶׁת יָמִ֗ים יִשָּׂ֤א פַרְעֹה֙ אֶת־רֹאשֶׁ֔ךָ וַהֲשִֽׁיבְךָ֖ עַל־כַּנֶּ֑ךָ וְנָתַתָּ֤ כוֹס־פַּרְעֹה֙ בְּיָד֔וֹ כַּמִּשְׁפָּט֙ הָֽרִאשׁ֔וֹן אֲשֶׁ֥ר הָיִ֖יתָ מַשְׁקֵֽהוּ׃

i18n.en: within yet three days shall Pharaoh lift up thy head, and restore thee unto thine office: and thou shalt give Pharaoh's cup into his hand, after the former manner when thou wast his butler.

notes.official: *Yissa Par'oh et-roshekha* ('Pharaoh shall lift up thy head') deploys the idiom *nasa rosh* in its **favorable** sense — to raise from disgrace, restore to honor and office. The closest HB parallel is 2 Kgs 25:27 (= Jer 52:31), where the Babylonian king 'lifted up the head of Jehoiachin' = released him from prison and restored his dignity — almost exactly the cupbearer's situation. This positive use is set up here precisely so that v 19 can reverse it punningly against the baker. Governed by `nasa-rosh-lift-up-the-head-idiom`; the idiom is rendered uniformly across vv 13, 19, 20 so the wordplay survives in English.

paragraphs.text: כִּ֧י אִם־זְכַרְתַּ֣נִי אִתְּךָ֗ כַּאֲשֶׁר֙ יִ֣יטַב לָ֔ךְ וְעָשִֽׂיתָ־נָּ֥א עִמָּדִ֖י חָ֑סֶד וְהִזְכַּרְתַּ֙נִי֙ אֶל־פַּרְעֹ֔ה וְהוֹצֵאתַ֖נִי מִן־הַבַּ֥יִת הַזֶּֽה׃

i18n.en: But have me in thy remembrance when it shall be well with thee, and show kindness, I pray thee, unto me, and make mention of me unto Pharaoh, and bring me out of this house:

notes.official: Solitary *chesed* — *ve-asita-na imadi chesed* ('and show kindness, I pray thee, unto me') — rendered ASV-baseline **kindness** per `chesed-solitary-covenant-kindness` (the covenant-loyalty / steadfast-love range, Glueck/Sakenfeld, documented there; *appliesTo* extended to add this verse, the second solitary-*chesed* occurrence in the corpus after Gen 39:21). Yosef's doubled *zekhartani* ('remember me') / *hizkartani* ('make mention of me') sets up the remember-forget hinge that the chapter closes on at v 23 (where the cupbearer does *not* remember), suspending Yosef until the cupbearer finally remembers at Gen 41:9.

paragraphs.text: כִּֽי־גֻנֹּ֣ב גֻּנַּ֔בְתִּי מֵאֶ֖רֶץ הָעִבְרִ֑ים וְגַם־פֹּה֙ לֹא־עָשִׂ֣יתִֽי מְא֔וּמָה כִּֽי־שָׂמ֥וּ אֹתִ֖י בַּבּֽוֹר׃

i18n.en: for indeed I was stolen away out of the land of the Ivrim: and here also have I done nothing that they should put me into the dungeon.

notes.official: Two terms. (a) *Me-eretz ha-Ivrim* ('out of the land of the Ivrim') — the gentilic *Ivri* used by an Israelite to foreigners about himself, the characteristic outsider-designation pattern; governed by `ha-ivri-hebrew-etymology` (the Eber / *habiru* / *eber*-'beyond' etymology-dispute documented there). This entry's Gen 40 ref is normalized from the legacy bare `GEN-40:15` to the corpus `GEN-WOH-40:15` form (consistent with the Gen 39 normalization). (b) *Ba-bor* ('into the dungeon') — Yosef calls his Egyptian **prison** a *bor*, the **same noun** as the dry cistern into which his brothers cast him at Gen 37:20-29. This is a deliberate verbal echo: the *bor* of the brothers' pit and the *beit ha-sohar* of the Egyptian prison are bound by Yosef's own retrospective vocabulary. The Yosef-cycle prison-lexicon thus spans three terms — *bor* (Gen 37; here), *beit ha-sohar* (Gen 39-40), and *beit ha-bor* ('house of the pit', 41:14) — and the Gen 37 `bor-pit-cistern-dry-water-shaft` entry's *appliesTo* is extended to add Gen 40:15 (its rationale already named this verse). ASV-baseline 'dungeon' retained on the surface (the same lemma the Gen 37 entry renders 'pit').

paragraphs.text: וַיַּ֥רְא שַׂר־הָאֹפִ֖ים כִּ֣י ט֣וֹב פָּתָ֑ר וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ אֶל־יוֹסֵ֔ף אַף־אֲנִי֙ בַּחֲלוֹמִ֔י וְהִנֵּ֗ה שְׁלֹשָׁ֛ה סַלֵּ֥י חֹרִ֖י עַל־רֹאשִֽׁי׃

i18n.en: When the chief baker saw that the interpretation was good, he said unto Yosef, I also was in my dream, and, behold, three baskets of white bread were on my head:

notes.official: *Ki tov patar* ('that the interpretation was good', the verb *p-t-r*; `pitron-dream-interpretation-yosef-cycle`). *Sallei chori* ('baskets of *chori*') — *chori* is a **hapax legomenon** (occurs only here in the HB) of contested sense: traditionally **'white bread'** (related to *chur*, 'white'; ASV/KJV/NJPS; LXX 'of fine bread'; ASV margin 'white baskets'), but also read as open-weave **'wicker' baskets** (from *chor*, 'hole') — which would suit the birds reaching the bread in v 17. ASV-baseline 'baskets of white bread' retained; the readings are documented, not adjudicated, in the overlay entry `sallei-chori-baskets-of-white-bread-hapax-gen40`.

paragraphs.text: וּבַסַּ֣ל הָֽעֶלְי֔וֹן מִכֹּ֛ל מַאֲכַ֥ל פַּרְעֹ֖ה מַעֲשֵׂ֣ה אֹפֶ֑ה וְהָע֗וֹף אֹכֵ֥ל אֹתָ֛ם מִן־הַסַּ֖ל מֵעַ֥ל רֹאשִֽׁי׃

i18n.en: and in the uppermost basket there was of all manner of baked food for Pharaoh; and the birds did eat them out of the basket upon my head.

paragraphs.text: וַיַּ֤עַן יוֹסֵף֙ וַיֹּ֔אמֶר זֶ֖ה פִּתְרֹנ֑וֹ שְׁלֹ֙שֶׁת֙ הַסַּלִּ֔ים שְׁלֹ֥שֶׁת יָמִ֖ים הֵֽם׃

i18n.en: And Yosef answered and said, This is the interpretation thereof: the three baskets are three days;

paragraphs.text: בְּע֣וֹד ׀ שְׁלֹ֣שֶׁת יָמִ֗ים יִשָּׂ֨א פַרְעֹ֤ה אֶת־רֹֽאשְׁךָ֙ מֵֽעָלֶ֔יךָ וְתָלָ֥ה אוֹתְךָ֖ עַל־עֵ֑ץ וְאָכַ֥ל הָע֛וֹף אֶת־בְּשָׂרְךָ֖ מֵעָלֶֽיךָ׃

i18n.en: within yet three days shall Pharaoh lift up thy head from off thee, and shall hang thee on a tree; and the birds shall eat thy flesh from off thee.

notes.official: The grim reversal of the v 13 idiom. *Yissa Par'oh et-roshekha* — the identical 'lift up thy head' — is here weaponized by the added *me-alekha* ('**from off thee**'): the head is still 'lifted', but lifted off; the clause continues *ve-talah otkha al-etz* ('and shall hang thee on a tree') and the birds eat the flesh. The pun depends on rendering vv 13 and 19 with the same English idiom ('lift up thy head'); differentiating them ('restore to office' v 13 / 'behead' v 19) would destroy the wordplay the Hebrew builds, so the ASV-baseline uniform rendering is retained. Governed by `nasa-rosh-lift-up-the-head-idiom`.

paragraphs.text: וַיְהִ֣י ׀ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַשְּׁלִישִׁ֗י י֚וֹם הֻלֶּ֣דֶת אֶת־פַּרְעֹ֔ה וַיַּ֥עַשׂ מִשְׁתֶּ֖ה לְכָל־עֲבָדָ֑יו וַיִּשָּׂ֞א אֶת־רֹ֣אשׁ ׀ שַׂ֣ר הַמַּשְׁקִ֗ים וְאֶת־רֹ֛אשׁ שַׂ֥ר הָאֹפִ֖ים בְּת֥וֹךְ עֲבָדָֽיו׃

i18n.en: And it came to pass the third day, which was Pharaoh's birthday, that he made a feast unto all his servants: and he lifted up the head of the chief butler and the head of the chief baker among his servants.

notes.official: The narrator now uses the single idiom *va-yissa et-rosh* ('he lifted up the head') of **both** men together — *sar ha-mashqim* and *sar ha-ofim* — 'in the midst of his servants'. The one idiom resolves in opposite directions: restoration for the cupbearer (v 21), execution for the baker (v 22). The deliberate neutral-ambiguity at v 20 is the keystone of the chapter's *nasa rosh* wordplay (`nasa-rosh-lift-up-the-head-idiom`); the uniform English rendering across vv 13, 19, 20 preserves it. The court-titles are governed by `sar-ha-mashqim-sar-ha-ofim-chief-cupbearer-baker`.

paragraphs.text: וַיָּ֛שֶׁב אֶת־שַׂ֥ר הַמַּשְׁקִ֖ים עַל־מַשְׁקֵ֑הוּ וַיִּתֵּ֥ן הַכּ֖וֹס עַל־כַּ֥ף פַּרְעֹֽה׃

i18n.en: And he restored the chief butler unto his butlership again; and he gave the cup into Pharaoh's hand:

paragraphs.text: וְאֵ֛ת שַׂ֥ר הָאֹפִ֖ים תָּלָ֑ה כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר פָּתַ֛ר לָהֶ֖ם יוֹסֵֽף׃

i18n.en: but he hanged the chief baker: as Yosef had interpreted to them.

notes.official: *Ka'asher patar lahem Yosef* ('as Yosef had interpreted to them', the verb *p-t-r*; `pitron-dream-interpretation-yosef-cycle`) confirms both interpretations as exactly correct, validating Yosef's v 8 claim that *pitronim* belong to Elohim.

paragraphs.text: וְלֹֽא־זָכַ֧ר שַֽׂר־הַמַּשְׁקִ֛ים אֶת־יוֹסֵ֖ף וַיִּשְׁכָּחֵֽהוּ׃ (פ)

i18n.en: Yet did not the chief butler remember Yosef, but forgat him.

notes.official: The chapter closes on an emphatic remember-forget doublet: *ve-lo zakhar ... va-yishkachehu* ('did not **remember** ... but **forgat** him'), pairing *zakhar* (H2142) and *shakhach* (H7911). The doubling is not redundant but a deliberate narrative hinge: it answers — negatively — Yosef's twofold *zekhartani* / *hizkartani* plea of v 14, and suspends Yosef in prison for the two years until *zakhar* finally returns at Gen 41:9, where the cupbearer says *et-chata'ai ani mazkir ha-yom* ('I do remember my faults this day'). No glossary entry: the pairing is a literary cross-reference into Gen 41, surfaced here as a setup-note. (ASV-baseline 'remember' / 'forgat' preserves both verbs.)
